b:
My heart wanted
to write a letter
to wish her a happy birthday

The words that should have bloomed
like a flood through an open sluice
got caught
in a whirlpool of thought

A wish sprouted
to address her first
in the threefold Tamil
that shone from the golden-peaked Himalayas
to the Pothigai hills!

If I call her
"friend!",
she is just one
among many

If I say
"elder sister not born to my mother",
age
stands in the way

Chinamika, "great in anger"?
No!
Her?
Her anger
would scorch
even the Chithirai sun

Nuvali, "the eloquent"?
She is the queen of speech
only when she wants to speak

Nakuna, "the laughing tongue"?
No,
aren't the things
she scatters
when she laughs
pearls!

Mikalaval, "the exalted"?
She
gives a definition
to simplicity

Meeyaazh, "finer than the lute"?
What
she plays
are the strings of a violin

Avirol, "the radiant"?
Yes,
she is
the great light
of knowledge!

But
even within that
her
worth
cannot be contained

The moment you call,
she answers within calling distance
and clears your troubles

Since she is always
a "gaja" away,
shall I call her
……… ?
No!
She is one
who wants
a soft sound
even for hard consonants!

A word
was born
to address her:

"Dear
……….,"
note: The poet tries out old literary Tamil epithets for a woman (given here in transliteration with their meanings) and rejects or accepts each in turn. "Threefold Tamil" (muttamil) is Tamil as poetry, music and drama. Tamil grammar divides consonants into hard (vallinam) and soft (mellinam) sounds. The name in the last lines is left blank in the original.
